seoTitle: How to Add a Payment Method on Shopify Without an LLC
metaDescription: Learn how to add a working payment method on Shopify without a registered business, using personal verification and alternative gateways instead of an LLC.
intro: Not having an LLC or registered business shouldn't stop you from accepting payments on Shopify. This guide walks through where Shopify actually asks for that information, what it wants when you try to set up Shopify Payments as an individual, and the alternative gateways sitting one click away for anyone who'd rather not register a company yet. You'll see the exact form fields involved and the full list of alternate providers Shopify itself surfaces when Shopify Payments isn't the right fit.

steps.heading: Find the Payments settings in your Shopify admin
steps.body: From your Shopify admin, go to Settings and click Payments. This is where every payment option for your store lives — Shopify Payments front and center with an Activate button, and a line underneath reading "See all other providers" if you want to use a different payment provider on your store. The Payments page also lists supported methods that plug in alongside whichever gateway you choose, including PayPal with no transaction fee, which is worth activating regardless of what you decide for your primary gateway.

image.caption: The Shopify Payments settings page, with the Activate button front and center and a link below it to see all other providers.

steps.heading: See what Shopify Payments actually asks for
steps.body: Click Activate Shopify Payments and you'll move through a multi-step setup — step 2 of 4 asks for an Account representative, and this is where the business requirement shows up concretely: first name, last name, date of birth, and a Social Security Number, described as 9 digits used for tax filing and verification. This is a personal SSN field, not necessarily an EIN, which is exactly why individual sellers without an LLC can often still complete this form using their own identity rather than a business entity's. It's worth reading each field carefully here rather than assuming you're locked out just because you don't have a registered company.

image.caption: Step 2 of the Shopify Payments setup, the Account representative form asking for personal details including a Social Security Number.

steps.heading: Browse alternative payment providers if you'd rather not use Shopify Payments
steps.body: Back on the Payments page, the "See all other providers" link opens a long list of third-party gateways Shopify already supports out of the box — names like Antom, Appmax, authorize.net, Clover Payments, dLocal Go Credit Cards, and MyFatoorah, each showing which card networks and regional payment types they support. These exist precisely for sellers who can't or don't want to go through Shopify Payments' business verification, and several are built around individual or regional merchant accounts rather than requiring a US-style LLC. Scroll through a few of these and check their own onboarding requirements before committing, since verification rules vary by provider and by country.

image.caption: The full list of alternative payment providers Shopify supports, each showing its supported card networks and regional payment types.

steps.heading: Gather your personal documents before applying
steps.body: Whichever route you take — Shopify Payments with a personal SSN or a third-party gateway aimed at individuals — have your government-issued ID and bank account details ready before you start the application. Providers process these applications faster when the name on your ID, the name on your bank account, and the name you type into the form all match exactly. A mismatch here, even a minor one like a missing middle initial, is one of the most common reasons an application stalls in review.

steps.heading: Avoid the mistakes that cause approval delays
steps.body: Beyond matching names, double-check that your bank account accepts the currency and country the gateway expects, and that any address you enter matches your ID rather than a forwarding or virtual address if the provider checks for that. Submitting an application with obviously mismatched or incomplete information tends to trigger manual review, which can add days or weeks compared to an application that sails through automated checks. If a provider does flag your account, most offer a support channel to resubmit documents rather than starting over from scratch.

faq.question: Can I really accept payments on Shopify without an LLC?
faq.answer: Yes. Shopify Payments' own setup form asks for a personal Social Security Number for tax verification, which individual sellers can use, and Shopify also supports a long list of third-party gateways built for individual and regional merchants.

faq.question: What documents do I need without a registered business?
faq.answer: You'll typically still need a government ID and bank account information, even without LLC paperwork, plus a Social Security Number if you go the Shopify Payments route.

faq.question: Where do I find alternative payment providers if Shopify Payments doesn't fit?
faq.answer: On the Payments page in Settings, click "See all other providers" beneath the Shopify Payments activation panel to see the full list, including options like authorize.net, Clover Payments, and dLocal.

faq.question: Why does my Shopify payment application get delayed?
faq.answer: Delays usually happen when the name, address, or bank details you submit don't exactly match your ID, or when documents are incomplete — double-checking details before applying helps avoid manual review.
